question: Does EMA's two-decimal published output for Data set II distinguish df 19.603 from df 22.540 at all?

assumed_standard_error.basis: Agreed to every digit shown by nlme, glmmTMB and ReplicateBE.jl - three independent fits. NOT published by EMA. See VAL-FDA-APPENDIX-C-001 and -002.

df_range_compatible_with_two_decimal_rou.method: log(U/L)/2 depends only on the ratio of the published limits, so the point estimate and its rounding do not enter. Each extreme of the admissible half-width inverts to one end of a df interval; t is decreasing in df, so the widest half-width gives the smallest df.

df_range_that_reprints_all_three_publish.method: Scan of df, keeping those for which estimate, lower and upper all round to the published two decimals.

union_over_every_estimate_that_prints_as.why: The strict window moves with the point estimate, and the true estimate is unknown - EMA printed 102.26, the fits give 102.2644. Fixing either would be a choice; the union over the rounding band is not.

df_inverted_from_published_ci.note: NOT a published df. It is one inversion of rounded output against an unpublished SE, and has been quoted to three decimals throughout this project.
